name: WY at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Wyoming's R+23 partisan lean makes any Democratic win extremely unlikely
Republican Chuck Gray holds a massive fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000 with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win probability near 98%
model.rationale: Wyoming's R+23 lean makes this open seat effectively unwinnable for Democrats, and the resource gap is overwhelming: Gray has raised $1.6 million with $1.6 million in outside support, while Kinney has raised under $20,000. Markets price a Republican win at roughly 98%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: A major scandal or independent expenditure surge against Gray could narrow the margin, though it would be unlikely to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Harriet Hageman (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Wyoming's at-large House seat is among the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+23. With incumbent Harriet Hageman leaving the seat to run for Senate, Republican Chuck Gray enters the general election as the heavy favorite. He has raised about $1.6 million and benefits from roughly $1.6 million in outside support, plus $724,000 in outside spending opposing him that appears aimed at the primary field rather than the general election.

Democrat Lisa Kinney has raised under $20,000 and has no outside backing, leaving her with minimal resources to compete statewide. Prediction markets give Republicans about a 98% chance of holding the seat. The forecast calls the race Safe Republican, with Gray expected to win by roughly 20 points.
